comments.value: are you talking about the upload screen (in the game tab), the reason it lags a bit is because unity builds a complete scene in real time (skybox/your model(including all components)/the upload ui and its scripts with a delay set by unity itself for other scripts to process stuff in the background)

The window itself will cause lag when it runs the checks on the various avatars that use the descriptor. If you have many avatars active with a descriptor it will probably cause more lag. If your system can't check everything fast enough it may lag (obviously). If the build window update rate is high this could cause consistent lag whenever the window is open or opened.

Unless something was changed in the new sdk that altered the update rate, I would at this point assume your computer is not too powerful and or your unity scene is not optimal for how the build panel checks avatars.

Off the top of my head adding it to the descriptor would probably incur the same performance hit as each active descriptor would be running its own checks similar to how the build panel already does for all descriptors.

@{5ab3ad272b67505f726c2a8f|full_name}: Its nothing new in this version, I was experiencing this before aswell.  I simply explained an alternative way of the upload button being in the descriptor instead of all upload buttons being in the same tab because, if my rig (i7 8700k + rx vega 64) gets a lag spike at random times when the build control panel is open, and a lot of people have less powerful rigs they model with, I'm sure I'm not the only person experiencing these hitches.  So the alternative would theoretically help a lot of people, afterall there is no reason for it to check EVERYTHING on EVERY model every few seconds, only needs to check it when actually uploading a specific model.
@{5b9ab9ce22d5f33c2c26c00f|full_name}: I'm talking about the Build control panel (Where you click Build and upload) that launches the game tab setup screen.

@{5b7f976e561777408ec1cd56|full_name}: okay, I looked through the code again just so I could respond properly this time. Checking the avatars only happens once on each Unity editor event OnFocus and OnLostFocus. The lag spike is because it clears all Issues and checks the avatars again in a single GUI update. 

I was mistaken before when when I mentioned the constant updating. The constant updating does repaint the window but will only check avatars on the specified focus events. 

I see no reason to change the checking behaviour now that I have double check how it works. If you are constantly putting the window into focus you will get that lag spike as it rechecks the avatars for a single frame. This means you might want to reorganise where you have the window, or only open it when you need to publish.

@{5ab3ad272b67505f726c2a8f|full_name}: It still has a hitch on some systems, and hitching should be avoided as much as possible in my opinion.  There is still no reason for it to check or even display every models checks all the time.  I cant even open the Build Control panel without unity locking up, and that's with just 2 or 3 models with the descriptor on them.  If the checks only happened on request, or just before upload, this would be easily avoided.  There really is not much reason to have it displayed for every descriptor constantly.

@{5b7f976e561777408ec1cd56|full_name}: A single manager to handle everything is a much better practice then individual methods.  Whether its 1 model or 17 at once like I tested, it is still only doing it when you focus or lose focus on the window. Meaning it is already on demand and you only open it once you are ready to upload so that covers that situation. 

You also need to keep in mind that the usability design of the manager needs to take into account people of all Unity skill levels, and by design I can't fault it checking and displaying the information automatically for people who otherwise would not understand. Especially when it displays important information for setup. This situation means people can have it open while learning what is needed to upload, for example an avatar, to vrchat and then later on only focus the window when they require to upload or update something as they already know what to do, like in your situation.

If I was to currently redo the build manager all I would do is remove the OnLostFocus event because that would be when most people would notice the performance hitch and its a redundant recheck of the issues when a user has already interacted with the manager. might also look at running the checks in a coroutine or similar, but its not always worth the hassle. 

I don't know if they have already tried a setup with individual refresh buttons but for now you need to consider how a wide range of people will use and understand how Unity and the sdk work. I am willing to edit the code, you understand why the check causes a hitch, what will someone with no Unity knowledge do when you start hiding information behind extra steps or start complicating the descriptors even more with all the login and upload information. One handy manager to both view and control uploads with automatic display of crucial information sounds, and in practice is, good enough for its use case.

details:
I recently found that my unity lags for a few seconds, not accepting any input.  This only happens when the VRC Build Control panel is open.  
As this is more of a request since I don't see many with this issue and its not a horrible issue, My proposed change is get rid of the Build Control Panel entirely, and instead embed the "Upload" button into the Avatar Descriptor (Similarly move the World build buttons to the Scene descriptor)
This will both make using unity not lag for me (And I'm sure others) and make it simpler for people who are new to uploading avatars.
title: SDK - Move the Upload button to the VRC descriptor
